issues.failure_explanation: As written, (eq:ivp_ode_weak) imposes the initial condition strongly while testing the residual against all N+1 basis functions. The stiffness matrix K_{pq} = \int \varphi_p \varphi_q' is singular (K 1 = 0 since \sum_q \varphi_q \equiv 1), so for a general F the N+1 Galerkin equations are inconsistent (\mu F is generically outside the range of K) even before the extra constraint q_n(0) = u_n: the stated problem has no solution and does not define the local solution. The algebraic system the paper actually uses, (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst) with \kappa_{pq} = \psi_p\psi_q + \int\varphi_p\varphi_q' and right-hand side \psi_p u_n, is the discretization of the standard weak (jump) imposition \varphi_p(0)(q_n(0) - u_n) + \int \varphi_p (q_n' - \Delta t_n F) = 0, which is missing from (eq:ivp_ode_weak). The paper itself later proves that the computed local solution satisfies q_n(0) != u_n for general F (Remark lemma:p_ode_exact:remark:rado_l), directly contradicting the stated strong equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the weak form with the standard weak imposition of the initial condition, \varphi_p(0)(q_n(0) - u_n) + \int_0^1 \varphi_p(\tau)[dq_n/d\tau - \Delta t_n F(q_n(\tau), t(\tau))]d\tau = 0, dropping the strong equality q_n(0) = u_n; this is exactly the form whose discretization is (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst).
issues.overall_effect: The defining weak problem of the local DG predictor is ill-posed as written (overdetermined, generically unsolvable) and internally inconsistent with a later remark. The algebraic scheme (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst), (eq:snae_lstdg) on which every theorem rests is correct, so no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Weak form of the local DG predictor omits the initial-condition jump term; as stated the problem is generically unsolvable and contradicts the later result q_n(0) != u_n
issues.why_classification: The fix is the standard one-line jump term of DG/ADER-DG local predictors, already implicit in the matrix \kappa and in the paper's own Remark rado_l; every downstream claim uses the correct algebraic system, so all results survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With a = \kappa^{-1}\mu, the identity a\psi = w is equivalent to \mu\psi = \kappa w, i.e. w_p\psi_p = \sum_q \kappa_{pq} w_q, which does not follow from and is not equivalent to the (correct) relations \kappa^{-1}\psi = 1 \Leftrightarrow \psi = \kappa 1 stated next to it; the asserted chain of equivalences holds only when all weights are equal (N = 1). Direct evaluation from the paper's definitions for N = 2 (\tau = {1/2-\sqrt{15}/10, 1/2, 1/2+\sqrt{15}/10}, w = {5/18, 4/9, 5/18}) gives [a\psi] \approx (0.2979, 0.2083, 0.1688), whereas w \approx (0.2778, 0.4444, 0.2778): the relation already fails for N = 2. Hence the terminal '= w_p' in the first line of the proof is an invalid inference. The remaining relations (2)-(7) of (eq:ader_int_prop) are correct (verified by the same direct computation).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the relation \sum_q a_{pq}\psi_q = w_p from (eq:ader_int_prop) and restrict the equivalence chain to the valid pair \sum_q[\kappa^{-1}]_{pq}\psi_q = 1 \Leftrightarrow \psi_p = \sum_q\kappa_{pq}.
issues.overall_effect: One of the seven parameter identities collected in Lemma ader_int_prop is false and its proof contains an unjustified final equality. The false identity is never used later (applications of the lemma use only the correct relations \sum_q[\kappa^{-1}]_{pq}\psi_q = 1 in (eq:snae_lstdg) and \sum_p a_{pq}\tilde\psi_p = w_q in (eq:ader_dg_node_sol_by_q)), so nothing else is affected.
issues.title: The relation \sum_q a_{pq}\psi_q = w_p in Lemma ader_int_prop is false for N >= 2, and the claimed equivalence with the correct relations fails
issues.why_classification: A false but unused identity: removing it and correcting the equivalence chain is a local edit that preserves every downstream claim, since all applications of the lemma rely on its other, correct relations.

where $a_{pq}$ is elements of the matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\mu$, and Lemma~\ref{lemma:ader_int_prop} is taken into account.

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own definition a = \kappa^{-1}\mu with \kappa from (eq:kappa_mu_defs), for N = 1 (\psi = ((1+\sqrt3)/2, (1-\sqrt3)/2), \mu = (1/2)I) one obtains a = [[1/3, (1-\sqrt3)/6], [(1+\sqrt3)/6, 1/3]]. The printed table has a_{12} = -(1-\sqrt3)/2 = (\sqrt3-1)/2 \approx 0.366 and a_{21} = (1-\sqrt3)/2 \approx -0.366 instead of (1-\sqrt3)/6 \approx -0.122 and (1+\sqrt3)/6 \approx 0.455. The printed row sums, 1/3 \pm (\sqrt3-1)/2, do not equal the abscissae 1/2 \mp \sqrt3/6, so the table violates the condition \sum_q a_{pq} = \tau_p (the r = 0 case of C(N), explicitly highlighted in the paper) and cannot be the two-stage method of order 3 established in Theorem order_rk. The N = 2 table in the same display checks out correctly against a = \kappa^{-1}\mu, so the error is isolated to the N = 1 off-diagonal entries.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two off-diagonal entries by a_{12} = (1-\sqrt3)/6 and a_{21} = (1+\sqrt3)/6, as dictated by a = \kappa^{-1}\mu.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed N = 1 Butcher table does not represent the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method and contradicts the paper's own simplifying-condition and order results; the table is illustrative and no result depends on it.
issues.title: The printed N = 1 Butcher table has wrong off-diagonal entries and violates the row-sum condition C(1) proved in the paper
issues.why_classification: An isolated, concrete numerical error in an illustrative display with no dependents; the correction is forced by the paper's definitions and changes no claim or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Numerical investigation of cases $N = 1, \ldots, 75$ showed that conditions $C(N)$, $D(N)$ are satisfied with precision $10^{-978}$--$10^{-1006}$. However, conditions $C(N+1)$, $D(N+1)$, which are inherent in the classical GL method are not satisfied, but the deviations decrease with $N$, reaching $10^{-48}$--$10^{-49}$ for $C(N+1)$ and $10^{-50}$--$10^{-52}$ for $D(N+1)$ in case $N = 75$.

The IRK-GL-ADER-DG method is not a collocation method according to Theorem 7.7 in~\cite{Hairer_book_1}, since it has the convergence order $p_{\rm RK} > s$ and the simplifying condition $C(N+1)$ is not satisfied.

issues.failure_explanation: Butcher's theorem applied to B(2N+2), C(N), D(N) with s = N+1 stages yields order at least min(2N+2, N+N+1, 2N+2) = 2N+1, i.e. a lower bound. The statement asserts the order equals 2N+1 (stressed in the text as 'one unit less' than the 2s = 2N+2 of the Gauss method), which requires excluding order 2N+2. The standard argument — an s-stage method of order 2s is necessarily the Gauss collocation method, which satisfies C(N+1) = C(s), whereas here C(N+1) fails — is never made; the failure of C(N+1) and D(N+1) is documented only by high-precision floating-point checks for N = 1,...,75. Corollary rk_is_not_coll likewise asserts non-collocation for arbitrary N from this unproven premise. Hence, as written, for general N the proof establishes materially less (order >= 2N+1) than the statement (order = 2N+1).

failure_location.quote: The approximation order of the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method is $p_{\rm RK} = 2N + 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove analytically that C(N+1) (and D(N+1)) fails for every N: extending the alternative proof of Lemma cn_cond to r = N gives the residual -w_p\prod_{q\neq p}(\tau_p-\tau_q)/(N+1) \neq 0, because \tau^{N+1} is not reproduced by interpolation in span{\varphi_q}; then invoke the classical uniqueness of the s-stage Gauss method among methods of order 2s to cap the order at 2N+1.
issues.overall_effect: The exact approximation/superconvergence order p_RK = p_G = 2N+1 at grid nodes (repeated in the abstract, Corollary order_ader_dg_nodes, and the conclusion) and the non-collocation Corollary rk_is_not_coll are rigorously supported only as 'order at least 2N+1' for arbitrary N; for N > 75 there is no evidence at all.
issues.title: Theorem order_rk asserts the exact order 2N+1, but the argument proves only order >= 2N+1; the needed failure of C(N+1)/D(N+1) is supported only numerically for N <= 75
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the missing piece is contained (one extra case of the paper's own alternative-proof computation plus a classical uniqueness theorem), but it is a genuinely new analytic ingredient: as written, the central exact-order claim for arbitrary N and the non-collocation corollary rest on numerical evidence for N <= 75, so more than a local or routine repair is required.

issues.failure_explanation: Since \tilde u is the exact solution on \Omega_n started from the numerical value \tilde u(t_n) = u_n, the quantity |\tilde u(t_n) - u(t_n)| = |u_n - u(t_n)| is the accumulated global error of the nodal solution at t_n, which for a method of order p_RK = 2N+1 is O(\Delta t^{2N+1}) — exactly the nodal superconvergence order the paper proves (Corollary order_ader_dg_nodes) and measures empirically. The proof instead bounds it by C_app \Delta t_n^{2N+2}, the one-step local truncation error, which equals the nodal error only on the first element; for n >= 1 the displayed inequality is false. The accompanying sentence ('2N+2 in the exponent ... at one step \varepsilon = O(\Delta t_n^{p_RK+1})') shows the local and global errors are being conflated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by |u_n - u(t_n)| <= C_app \Delta t^{2N+1} (the global error of a method of order 2N+1, \Delta t = max_n \Delta t_n); the rest of the estimate is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: An intermediate inequality in the proof of Lemma local_sol_order_L_inf is false as written. The lemma's conclusion is unaffected, because the corrected global-error term O(\Delta t^{2N+1}) is still absorbed by the O(\Delta t_n^{N+1}) interpolation term.
issues.title: In Lemma local_sol_order_L_inf the global nodal error |u_n - u(t_n)| is bounded by the one-step local truncation error O(\Delta t_n^{2N+2})
issues.why_classification: A one-inequality correction whose correct exponent still exceeds N+1, so the statement, the method, and all downstream conclusions survive verbatim with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The local solution $\mathbf{q}_{n}$ is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial of degree $N$ (\ref{eq:local_sol}) whose coefficients $\{\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{p}\}_{p = 0}^{N}$ are the solution of the system of equations (\ref{eq:snae_lstdg}), where $\mathbf{u}_{n}$ is known with the approximation order $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The classical remainder formula bounds ||I_N \tilde u - \tilde u||_\infty, where I_N \tilde u is the interpolant on the exact nodal values \tilde u(t_n + \tau_p \Delta t_n). But q_n = \sum_p \hat q_{n,p} \varphi_p is built from the solution of the nonlinear stage system (eq:snae_lstdg), and \hat q_{n,p} \neq \tilde u(t_n + \tau_p \Delta t_n) for a general smooth F (equality holds only in the polynomial situation of Lemma p_ode_exact, which therefore cannot justify the bound 'for sufficiently smooth F'). The displayed estimate is thus applied to a polynomial that is not the interpolant of \tilde u. The missing ingredient is a stage-error estimate |\hat q_{n,p} - \tilde u(t_n + \tau_p\Delta t_n)| = O(\Delta t_n^{N+1}) — which follows from the proven condition C(N) (Lemma cn_cond) together with Lipschitz stability of the stage system — combined with the decomposition q_n - \tilde u = \sum_p(\hat q_{n,p} - \tilde u(t_{n,p}))\varphi_p + (I_N\tilde u - \tilde u) and the Lebesgue constant of the fixed Gauss-Legendre nodes. The conclusion (order N+1) is correct, but the proof given does not establish it.

issues.title: Lemma local_sol_order_L_inf applies the Lagrange interpolation error formula to q_n although its nodal values are RK stage approximations, not exact values of the exact solution; the stage-error estimate is missing
issues.why_classification: The claim survives and the additional argument is standard and contained (no new global proof architecture and no weakening of the statement), but a real, nontrivial step — the stage-error analysis — must be supplied, since the proof's key estimate is simply not applicable to q_n.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $\mathrm{M}$ (\ref{eq:q_m_matrices_def}) is non-negative definite by Lemma~\ref{lemma:q_m_matrices_posdef}, and matrix $\mu$ (\ref{eq:kappa_mu_defs}) is positive definite, so the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method is algebraically stable, by Definition~4.2.1 in~\cite{Dekker_Verwer_1984}.

issues.failure_explanation: The implication 'algebraically stable => BN-stable' cited from Dekker-Verwer (Theorem 4.2.2, the Burrage-Butcher theorem) is stated for irreducible Runge-Kutta methods; reducible algebraically stable methods need not be BN-stable. The paper establishes algebraic stability (M non-negative definite, w_p > 0) but never states or verifies irreducibility (DJ- and HS-irreducibility), so the cited theorem is applied with an unestablished hypothesis. The hypothesis is in fact satisfied here — a = \kappa^{-1}\mu is invertible, so a has no zero column, which with w_p > 0 gives DJ-irreducibility, and distinct rows of a give HS-irreducibility — but no such observation appears in the paper.

failure_location.quote: The IRK-GL-ADER-DG method is $BN$-stable by the Theorem~4.2.2 in~\cite{Dekker_Verwer_1984}, and $B$-stable as a special case.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the observation that a is invertible with positive weights and distinct abscissae, hence the method is DJ- and HS-irreducible, after which Theorem 4.2.2 applies as cited.
issues.overall_effect: The BN-stability of the method — and with it the aggregate stability statement for the ADER-DG method (Corollary coroll:ader_dg_stabs) and the corresponding abstract/conclusion claims — rests on a theorem applied outside its verified hypotheses.
issues.title: Corollary b_bn_stab_rk derives BN-stability from algebraic stability without verifying the irreducibility hypothesis of the cited Dekker-Verwer theorem
issues.why_classification: The omitted hypothesis is true and follows from a routine one-line check based on properties already established in the paper (invertibility of a, w_p > 0, distinct Gauss nodes); no claim, regime, or rate changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore $\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{I} - \boldsymbol{\psi}\mathbf{1}^{T}) = N$, and $\mathrm{rank}(a - \mathbf{1}\mathbf{w}^{T}) = N$. Therefore the numerator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $P_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N-1$. It follows that $R(z)$ is the $(N, N+1)$-Pad\'{e} approximation $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of $\exp(z)$.

R(z) = 1 + \mathbf{w}^{T} z \left[\mathrm{I} - za\right]^{-1} \mathbf{1} = 
\frac{\mathrm{I} - za + z \mathbf{1}\mathbf{w}^{T}}{\mathrm{I} - za} = \frac{P_{N, N+1}(z)}{R_{N, N+1}(z)}.

By Theorem~3.11 in~\cite{Hairer_book_2}, the residual term of the $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ is $\exp(z) - R_{N, N+1}(z) = O(z^{2N+2})$, so the approximation order of the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$, which is an alternative proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:order_rk}.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The denominator det(I - za) has degree N+1, not N: a is an invertible (N+1)x(N+1) matrix, so all N+1 eigenvalues are nonzero. (ii) From rank(a - 1 w^T) = N one obtains only that the numerator det(I - z(a - 1w^T)) has degree at most N; the asserted 'degree N-1' neither follows nor is correct (already for N = 1 the actual numerator is the degree-1 polynomial 1 + z/3). The two stated degrees are also inconsistent with the claimed (N, N+1) Padé type, whose degrees are N and N+1. (iii) Degree bounds alone do not imply that a rational function is the (N, N+1)-Padé approximant of exp(z): one must additionally show R(z) - e^z = O(z^{2N+2}), which for a Runge-Kutta stability function is exactly the statement that the method has order 2N+1; this approximation argument is absent, so the proof's central inference is a non-sequitur. (iv) Consequently the only available completion uses Theorem order_rk, under which Corollary cor:added-3 — the Padé residual O(z^{2N+2}) as 'an alternative proof of Theorem order_rk' — is circular, unless an order-independent identification of R with the Padé fraction is supplied (the reported symbolic/numeric checks cover only N <= 6 and N <= 75). The scalar R(z) is also written as a quotient of matrices; the standard determinant ratio det(I - za + z 1 w^T)/det(I - za) is evidently intended. The conclusion of the theorem is nevertheless correct.

failure_location.quote: The matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\cdot\mu$ in the denominator is invertible and $\mathrm{rank}(a) = N+1$. The denominator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the degree statements (denominator of degree N+1 since a is invertible; numerator of degree at most, and in fact exactly, N), write R(z) as the determinant ratio, and add the missing approximation step: a method of order 2N+1 has R(z) = e^z + O(z^{2N+2}), so uniqueness of the (N, N+1)-Padé approximant identifies R with R_{N,N+1}. Then downgrade cor:added-3 to a consistency remark, or else establish the Padé identification independently of the order (e.g., by deriving R(z) - e^z = O(z^{2N+2}) directly from B(2N+2), C(N), D(N)).
issues.overall_effect: The identification of the stability function with the (N, N+1)-Padé approximant is unproven as written. The alternative A-stability proof (cor:added-2), the alternative order proof (cor:added-3), the L-stability theorem (whose |z|^{-1} asymptotics is read off the Padé degrees), and the aggregate stability claims for the ADER-DG method (coroll:ader_dg_stabs, abstract, conclusion) all lose their stated support. A-stability survives independently via AN-stability, and L-stability is independently repairable via R(infty) = 1 - w^T a^{-1} 1 = 0.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem pade_approx misstates numerator/denominator degrees and never proves the Padé approximation property; the 'alternative proof of order' in cor:added-3 becomes circular
issues.why_classification: The theorem's conclusion is true and is restored by standard ingredients, but the published proof contains two false degree statements and a non-sequitur as its central inference, and the least repair either withdraws the advertised 'alternative proof of order' in cor:added-3 or requires a new contained argument — more than a local fix, but without loss of the main stability conclusions.
